newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN PILE UP ASIA CUP RECORD TOTAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN PILE UP ASIA CUP RECORD TOTAL.

text.p: Pakistan, fired by 90 in 94 balls from opener Saeed Anwar, punished sloppy Bangladesh fielding to make the highest-ever Asia Cup total on Wednesday.
Pakistan made 319 for five in their 50 overs at the R.Premadasa stadium, beating their own previous record of 284 for three off 45 overs, also against Bangladesh, at Chittagong in 1988.
Anwar, leading the assault after Pakistan won the toss, struck 11 fours and shared a second wicket partnership of 123 in 121 balls with captain Ramiz Raja.
They repaired the early damage caused by losing opener Aamir Sohail without scoring. He lasted one ball before being caught behind.
Ramiz (52), Inzamam-ul-Haq (77) and Salim Malik (62 off 60 balls) all scored freely as the Bangladesh fielding wilted under the onslaught.
Anwar, who was hit on the left eye at 73 while attempting to sweep off-spinner Naimur Rahman, was dropped one run later by Habibul Basharat at long off.
However, he atoned for his laspe by catching Anwar in the same position after he had added another 17 runs.
Athar Ali put down a simple catch off Malik at mid-wicket when the batsman was on 42. Malik and Inzamam went on to a 109-run fourth wicket partnership in 95 balls.
